question.text: Which of the following statements about exchange-traded derivative contracts in India is correct?

answer.text: Section 18A of SCRA provides that derivative contracts are legal and valid only if traded on a recognized stock exchange and settled on its clearing house
All derivative contracts including OTC derivatives are governed by SCRA
Derivative contracts do not require clearing house settlement to be legally valid
Only equity derivatives are recognized under SCRA; commodity derivatives are governed separately

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 18A of SCRA provides that contracts in derivatives shall be legal and valid if: (1) traded on a recognized stock exchange, (2) settled on the clearing house of the recognized stock exchange, and (3) between such parties and on such terms as the Central Government may specify. The Trap: The three Section 18A conditions are cumulative; a derivative that does not meet them is not legal and valid under SCRA. Note: Pages 19-20 support the Section 18A validity conditions; specific OTC/RBI/ISDA framework claims are not stated in the pages checked.
